what: HIGH (code audit CA-A10-402, MEASURED 2026-09-27): zero of the 64 files under deploy/ declare OnFailure=, and scripts/ops/status_check.sh's exit code is gated on `systemctl is-active` for only 3 hardcoded long-running services (ict-trader-live, ict-web-api, ict-telegram-bot) -- its broader ict-* enumeration is explicitly documented as read-only, head-capped at 60 lines, and never affecting the exit code. So NO oneshot+timer pair in this repo (~41 declared ict-* units per the CA-A10 deploy-lane's count) has any alerting path for its own failure; a failed unit is visible only if a session or the operator happens to pull the right diag endpoint and specifically looks. This is the systemic cause behind the lead this lane was dispatched to check: ict-git-sync.service read 'failed' on 2026-09-27 (PI-20260927-YZRZQ725-0002, now closed -- see that record) while its timer stayed 'active' throughout, masking the failure from anything reading only timer state; a live re-pull this session caught a SECOND, independent, currently-failed instance of the exact same class (ict-ib-executions-pull.service, an IB Gateway connect refusal -- CA-A10-401/CA-A10-002 in this lane's findings file). Both were caught only by incidental diag reads, not by any purpose-built check. Full finding + evidence: docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-A10.findings.jsonl id CA-A10-402. Proposed fix: add `systemctl is-failed <unit>` (or a single `systemctl list-units --state=failed 'ict-*'` call) to status_check.sh's exit-code-gating logic for the money/deploy-freshness-adjacent oneshots at minimum.
